deities: Lord Shiva as Trilokinath (Lord of the Three Worlds, three-faced murti)
Ganesha, Kartikeya, Nandi, Narada, Sharda (in compound)

history.summary: Trilokinath Temple in Purani Mandi (Old Mandi), on the Beas River near the old Victoria Bridge, is one of Mandi's oldest temples and distinct from the more famous Hindu-Buddhist Triloknath shrine in Lahaul and Spiti — verify which one the CSV's 'Triloknath Temple' intends, though town=Mandi points to this one. Wikipedia and several sources credit Sultan Devi, queen of Raja Ajber Sen, with commissioning it around 1520 AD; templeyatri.in instead names Raja Ajber Sen himself (conflict). The square garbhagriha houses a three-faced Shiva image that gives the temple its name. It is a North-Indian Shikhara temple with carved pillars, wall images of Hindu deities, and a small water tank; it is under the jurisdiction of the Archaeological Survey of India. The CSV spelling 'Triloknath' is corrected to the documented 'Trilokinath'. Coordinates are POI-matched from map.geocode.

town_description: Mandi is a historic town on the Beas River and the headquarters of Mandi district, Himachal Pradesh. Known as 'Chhoti Kashi' (Varanasi of the Hills), it hosts some 81 old temples and is the venue of the famous Mandi Shivaratri Fair.

travel.railway: Joginder Nagar (narrow gauge) and Shimla (narrow gauge); broad-gauge connections at Chandigarh/Kalka
travel.road: About 1-2 km from Mandi bus station, across the old Victoria Bridge into Purani Mandi

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Maha Shivaratri for peak devotion
